signals.text: Revenue grew 17% a year over 3 years vs 23% over 5: growth is slowing.
Profit compounded at 8% vs revenue at 17%: profits are lagging sales.
Operating margin compressed 95 bps in 3 years (8.5% → 7.5%).
Over 5 years, operating cash flow was 105% of reported profit: profits are turning into cash.
Free cash flow was negative in 3 of the last 5 years: capex is running ahead of cash generation.

flags.text: Revenue grew 17% a year over 3 years vs 23% over 5: growth is slowing.
Profit compounded at 8% vs revenue at 17%: profits are lagging sales.
Free cash flow was negative in 3 of the last 5 years: capex is running ahead of cash generation.

guidance.statement: Open on an average every year at least 10% to 15% or maybe 10% to 20% of your base stores.
guidance.quote: Like we have always said that the right method of expansion in the offline space is to open on an average every year at least 10% to 15% or maybe 10% to 20% of your base stores – every year.

guidance.statement: We will not be less than 50 store openings next year.
guidance.quote: I mean, it won't be less than 50. I mean, if you're talking so much about it.

delivered.statement: Added 35.3 crores bill cuts in the year just gone by.
Like-for-like growth for 24 months plus stores was about 8.4%.
Added 2 million square feet of operating space and revenue from sales per square feet close to INR34,000.
Reported revenue of INR57,790 crores, EBITDA margin of 7.9%, and PAT margin of 5.1%.
Standalone sales grew by 16.7%, EBITDA grew by 10.8%, and PAT excluding tax gain grew by 7.3%.
Consolidated sales were about INR59,358 crores and PAT including tax was about INR2,707 crores at 4.6% margin.

calls.tone: confident on long-term offline retail and store expansion acceleration, cautious on short-term opex and quick commerce.

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned if DMart is underperforming peers due to rapid quick commerce growth and shrinking price advantages.
Analysts pressed on whether private labels and D2C brands should be accelerated faster to protect margins against rising real estate costs.
Analysts asked why return on capital employed and EBITDA margins have trended down over the last two years.
Analysts questioned why DMart Ready does not offer immediate delivery (30-60 mins) given market trends.

guidance.statement: We are primed and ready in terms of opening around 40-50 stores.
guidance.quote: We are primed and ready in terms of opening around 40-50 stores. I mean anything between that is what we are ready and we will deliver broadly.

guidance.statement: Store openings will be around 40 to 60 over the next three years.
guidance.quote: So you can take a range of 40 to 60 over the next three years.

guidance.statement: Blended gross margin will play around 14.5%, 15%, 15.5% ranges.
guidance.quote: I think 14.5%, 15%, 15.5%, those are the kind of ranges we play in from a gross margin standpoint.

guidance.statement: General merchandise and apparel contribution will trend around current run rates of around 23%.
guidance.quote: A broad trend line will be around the current run rates of around 23%, is the sense we get.

delivered.statement: Standalone revenue from operations reached INR 49,533 crores in FY24.
Standalone PAT delivered was INR 2,695 crores with a 5.4% PAT margin.
Opened 41 stores adding 1.8 million square feet of retail business area in FY24.
Delivered 30.3 crores bill cuts and a like-for-like growth of 9.9% in FY24.
Avenue E-commerce delivered INR 2,900 crores sales with a loss of INR 185 crores.

calls.tone: confident on core business model and long-term demand, cautious on quick commerce impact and margin expansion

pushback.gist: Analysts questioned the impact of quick commerce on metro revenues and potential strategy changes.
Analysts pressed on why store additions remain around 40 despite earlier targets of 15% to 20% growth.
Questions raised on persistent EBITDA losses and path to profitability for e-commerce.
Inquiries regarding the dip in general merchandise and apparel salience and recovery timeline.

guidance.statement: The company commits to open around 40 to 45 stores every year.
guidance.quote: we have that kind of inventory to at least commit saying 40-45, we will do, every year.

guidance.statement: Blended average gross margin is expected to range between 14.5% and 15.5%.
guidance.quote: I think 14.5%, 15%, 15.5%, those are the kind of ranges we play in from a gross margin standpoint.

guidance.statement: General merchandise and apparel contribution trend line will be around current run rates of around 23%.
guidance.quote: A broad trend line will be around the current run rates of around 23%, is the sense we get.

delivered.statement: Standalone revenue from operations reached INR49,533 crores in FY24.
Standalone EBITDA margin stood at 8.3% and PAT margin at 5.4% for FY24.
Delivered 30.3 crores bill cuts and 9.9% like-for-like growth in FY24.
Opened 41 stores adding 1.8 million square feet of retail business area in FY24.
Standalone PAT grew by 5.4% to INR2,695 crores in FY24.

calls.tone: Confident in core value model and apparel recovery, cautious on rapid store expansion and e-commerce profitability.

pushback.gist: Analysts repeatedly questioned why store expansion remains capped around 40-45 stores despite higher long-term aspirations.
Analysts pressed management on whether quick commerce is stealing metro customers and impacting store potential.
Questions raised on persistent EBITDA losses and the lack of a clear timeline for e-commerce breakeven.
Analysts probed why general merchandise and apparel mix has dipped and won't return to historical highs.

business.summary: Avenue Supermarts operates DMart retail stores providing everyday low prices through everyday low-cost operations, focusing primarily on food, non-food FMCG, and apparel.

bull.point: Company is practically debt-free (0.10 debt/equity), providing strong financial stability for growth.
Operating cash flow is robust, converting 105% of reported profit into cash over five years.

cite.table: Over 5 years, operating cash flow was 105% of reported profit

bull.point: Management opened 50 stores in FY25 and targets 15% annual store base growth.
Resilient core demand: like-for-like growth for stores open over 24 months was 8.1% in FY26.

bear.point: Revenue growth slowed to 17% over 3 years, down from 23% over 5 years.

cite.table: Revenue grew 17% a year over 3 years vs 23% over 5

bear.point: Profit growth of 8% significantly trails 17% revenue growth over three years.

cite.table: Profit compounded at 8% vs revenue at 17%

bear.point: DMart Ready losses widened to INR247 crores in FY25, with no clear profitability path.
Free cash flow was negative in 3 of the last 5 years due to high capex.

watch: Monitor if revenue growth continues to decelerate from 17% (3-year average).
Check if free cash flow turns positive, given it was negative in 3 of 5 years.
Track DMart Ready losses and any management timeline for achieving profitability.
